items.title: Pas members barred from backing Bersatu in Melaka polls
items.summary: Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party had confirmed it would contest at least one state seat in Melaka, where Bersatu was also fielding a candidate. Takiyuddin, who is also Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary-general, said yesterday that PN candidates would not clash with Umno or Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates in the Nov 14 election. He said PN members had been instructed to support BN candidates, while BN members could also choose to support PN candidates.

items.title: Johari: Careful tenant selection key to community safety
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Homeowners should exercise greater care when renting out their properties to prevent overcrowding and disputes that could affect the safety and well-being of local communities. Titiwangsa Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said problems could arise when homeowners who no longer lived in an area rented out their properties without properly considering the number of occupants and their suitability as tenants. Johari said maintaining public safety required close cooperation between the police, residents and community leaders, particularly in sharing information about potential risks.

items.title: Anwar chairs three major PKR meetings in Melaka before campaign launch
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 24 — Prime Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended three key party meetings held at around 3 pm today. The three important meetings, held at a hotel in Banda Hilir, comprised the State Leadership Council (MPN) meeting, the Central Political Bureau meeting and the PKR Central Leadership Council (MPP) meeting. Among the top party leaders who also attended the meetings were acting deputy president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, vice-president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh, Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim and Melaka Leadership Council chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim.

items.title: Two men found dead by riverbank after swimming in Sungai Tonggang
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 24 — Two men were found dead by a riverbank after swimming in a river, near Kampung Orang Asli Sungai Tonggang, Tanjung Rambutan, here today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant operations director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident involving two victims, aged 42 and 50, at 2.55 pm. “The rescue team then brought both victims out from across the river before the Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers confirmed their deaths at the scene,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Terengganu Sultan’s younger brother laid to rest
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 24 —The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, was laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum of Masjid Al-Muktafi Billah Shah here today. The funeral rites for Tengku Baderul Zaman, who died at the age of 52, were completed at 6.10 pm. The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, attended the funeral rites.

items.title: Selangor Sultan graces Royal Tea Reception in conjunction with Silver Jubilee celebration
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 24 —The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today graced a Royal Tea Reception attended by 1,500 retirees, investors and civil servants in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration of his reign at Istana Alam Shah here. Also in attendance were the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, and the Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah. At the event, Sultan Sharafuddin also launched the ‘Lakaran Indah Institusi Setiausaha Kerajaan Negeri Selangor’ book.

items.title: Terengganu Sultan's younger brother laid to rest
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, was laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum of Masjid Al-Muktafi Billah Shah here today. The funeral rites for Tengku Baderul Zaman, 52, concluded at 6.10pm. The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, attended the funeral, alongside Pahang's Tengku Ampuan, Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, who was accompanied by her children to convey their condolences to the Terengganu royal family.

items.title: Tun Faisal calls for Political Parties Act after PN deregistration row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should introduce a Political Parties Act to regulate political parties separately from other organisations under the Societies Act 1966. Tun Faisal said the proposed law should also require political parties to declare their assets, expenditure and political donations. Citing Kenya's Political Parties Act 2011, he said the country had established a selection committee comprising representatives of political parties, the legal fraternity and other stakeholders to oversee the appointment of its Registrar of Political Parties.

items.title: Yeo Bee Yin: Consult experts before deciding on nationwide Waze ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should consult industry experts and navigation technology specialists before deciding whether to impose a nationwide ban on Waze. Yeo said the proposed ban could affect more than six million road users who depend on real-time navigation. she said.

items.title: Two men drown in river near Tanjung Rambutan
items.summary: He said firefighters from the Tambun Fire and Rescue Station arrived at 3.28pm and found police personnel at the scene. Firefighters retrieved the men using stretchers, with personnel wearing personal flotation devices during the operation. Eight firefighters, supported by a fire rescue tender and an emergency medical rescue services vehicle, took part in the operation, alongside five police personnel and six Health Ministry personnel.

items.title: Public urged to stay calm during RTS Link security exercise on Oct 27
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 24 —The RTS Link Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Exercise Field Training Exercise (FTX) 2026 will be held at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar Station and Wadi Hana Depot in Johor Bahru on Tuesday (Oct 27). The National Security Council (MKN), Prime Minister’s Department, said the exercise would run from 9 am to 5 pm and be conducted in collaboration with Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd (MRTS Corp) and RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO). In a statement today, MKN said the exercise aimed to test and assess preparedness, response capabilities and coordination among Malaysian and Singaporean security agencies and emergency services.

items.title: Melaka polls: BN should not underestimate PN's strength, says Wawasan
items.summary: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) information chief Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal said PN had a solid support base in the state and could help BN shore up its position in seats where it had faced narrow victories in the previous election. "Our strength could help narrow that gap," he said. Commenting on PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan's statement that PN supporters had been asked to back BN candidates, while BN supporters could also support PN candidates, Wan Ahmad Fayhsal said Wawasan would extend similar support.

items.title: Teen killed in crash had bought birthday gifts for sister
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: A 16-year-old boy who died when a family car skidded and crashed into a tree in Bagan here last night had bought birthday gifts for his younger sister just hours before the tragedy. Putera Muhaimin Qudrat Mohd Noorwandi had bought the gifts during a family dinner outing in town, hoping to give them to his sister, Puteri Nur Fairuza Balqis, 15, when they returned home. His father, Mohd Noorwandi A Rahim, 41, said his son never got the chance to fulfil that wish.

items.title: Man dies buried in soil while hunting for gemstones
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 48-year-old man was killed after being buried under about one metre of soil while searching for gemstones near a water tank in Taman Kedidi, Pasir Gudang, today. Jamaluddin Wahab, from Taman Cahaya, Masai, was searching for gemstones with a friend at Jalan Kedidi 26 when the soil collapsed on him. Pasir Gudang Fire and Rescue Department station chief Firdaus Ahmad said a distress call was received at 10am.

items.title: Foreigner arriving from Penang held in Hong Kong with 2kg of cocaine
items.summary: Hong Kong Customs said in a statement yesterday that the drugs were discovered during an inspection of his luggage. Hong Kong Customs said it would step up enforcement against cross-border drug trafficking through intelligence analysis. Under Hong Kong's Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, drug trafficking carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment and a fine of HK$5 million (RM2.7 million) upon conviction.

items.title: SK Puchong Utama 2 team wins special award for RM114 pothole detector
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: On a budget of just RM114, a team of five pupils from SK Puchong Utama 2 proved that cost is no barrier to high-impact innovation, clinching the Special Award in the Digital Innovation Category at the 2026 Selangor State Metamorphosis appreciation ceremony yesterday. Known as Team Harmoni, the five Year Six pupils impressed the judges with their Pothole Detector On-The-Go, an Internet of Things (IoT)-based innovation that detects potholes in real time. Team member Syafierul Qaleef Shahrul Anuar, 12, said the idea for the device arose from a concern for road user safety and was also inspired by the school syllabus he had been learning since July.

items.title: Home Ministry leaves decision on charged AKPS chief to civil service process
items.summary: KULAI, Oct 24 — Matters concerning the position of Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain will be handled by the Home Ministry secretary-general and the Chief Secretary to the Government, said Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the matter was being handled by the two officials in accordance with existing public administration regulations. He was responding to questions on Mohd Shuhaily’s position as AKPS director-general while facing a court case.

items.title: Forest fires: Over 22,500ha remains under response in Indonesia
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia is continuing firefighting operations across approximately 22,595ha of forest and land, with Central Kalimantan accounting for the largest affected area. "In Kalimantan, the area still under response reached approximately 18,973ha comprising about 16,097ha in Central Kalimantan, 1,506ha in South Kalimantan, and 1,370ha in West Kalimantan. "In Sumatra, the area still under response reached approximately 2,431ha comprising about 2,050ha in South Sumatra, 379ha in Jambi, and 2ha in Riau," he said in a statement.

items.title: Johor schools to reopen on Monday as haze improves [WATCH]
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: All schools in Johor will reopen on Monday following an improvement in the haze situation, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings declining across the state over the past five days. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made at a meeting of the Johor State Disaster Management Committee, based on assessments by relevant agencies. He said changing wind directions, rising humidity and forecast rain were expected to help ease the haze, while health risk assessments by the Johor Health Department had been taken into account to safeguard pupils, teachers and school staff.

items.title: DAP’s Yeo warns nationwide Waze ban could disrupt logistics and gig economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — DAP national publicity secretary Yeo Bee Yin has cautioned the federal government against rushing into a blanket nationwide ban on the Waze navigation application, warning that a sudden prohibition would disrupt daily commutes, logistics, and gig-economy livelihoods for more than six million active Malaysian motorists. It directly impacts over six million active Malaysian road users who depend on real-time navigation daily for their livelihoods, commutes, and logistics,” she said in a statement. Waze has dismissed the data security allegations as "completely false", asserting that its global operations adhere to strict international privacy standards.

items.title: Govt targets 125,000 professional huffaz by 2050 - Zahid
items.summary: MELAKA: The government is confident of producing 125,000 professional huffaz by 2050 by expanding access to technical higher education, strengthening Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) and combining Quranic knowledge with professional and advanced technology skills. He said about 12,500 professional huffaz had been produced so far, while opportunities for tahfiz and pondok school students to pursue higher education at Universiti Kuala Lumpur (UniKL) and six universities under the Malaysian Technical Universities Network (MTUN) would be expanded from 2027. Zahid said clearer pathways into technical and professional higher education would enable huffaz to acquire specialised skills and professional qualifications to meet the country's future workforce needs.

items.title: Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian aid to Yemen - Mohamad
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian assistance to Yemen, while urging all parties in the protracted conflict in the country to return to the negotiation table and look for a diplomatic solution. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia empathises with the suffering of the Yemeni people who have to endure the effects of the protracted civil war, including famine and hardship in getting basic necessities. He said the matter was brought up by his counterpart, Yemen's Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, who shared on the latest developments in the country via a phone call on Thursday.

items.title: Police tracking down trio after men filmed riding atop moving Proton Wira
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police are tracking down the owner, driver and passengers of a blue Proton Wira after two men were filmed sitting on its roof as it moved along a road in Taman Puteri Wangsa, Ulu Tiram. Johor Baru Selatan district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said police detected the video and photographs at 9am today. He said the car was seen travelling from Jalan Beladau 32 towards Jalan Bukit Jaya.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysian company linked to ketamine-laden tanker seized in Indonesia
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the MT Global 168 was owned by a Johor Baru-based company with two Malaysian directors in their 40s and 50s. He said both directors had no previous criminal records and would be called in to assist investigations. "The vessel is registered under a company with two Malaysian directors, both in their 40s and 50s.

items.title: Two Malaysians injured in Typhoon Champi recovering in Taiwan hospitals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals who sustained minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi in Taiwan are receiving treatment at separate hospitals and their conditions are reported to be stable. Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC) President Bong Yik Jui said the two, both 57, were receiving treatment at Dali Jen Ai Hospital in Taichung and Miaoli Daqian Hospital in Miaoli, respectively. Bong said the MFTC would closely monitor developments related to Typhoon Champi, particularly its implications for the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan.

items.title: Two Malaysians injured by Typhoon Champi in stable condition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two Malaysians who sustained minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi in Taiwan are receiving treatment at separate hospitals and their conditions are reported to be stable. Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre, Taipei (MFTC) President Bong Yik Jui said the victims, both 57, were receiving treatment at Dali Jen Ai Hospital in Taichung and Miaoli Daqian Hospital in Miaoli, respectively. Bong said the MFTC would closely monitor developments related to Typhoon Champi, particularly its implications for the safety and welfare of Malaysians in Taiwan.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain, strong winds in nine states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 6 pm today. The warning covers Perlis, Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak), as well as Langkawi and Kubang Pasu in Kedah. The warning also applies to Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru in Johor; Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus and Setiu in Terengganu; and Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas and Tumpat in Kelantan.

items.title: Haze spreads to five Sarawak spots while Klang Valley air improves slightly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Air quality deteriorated further this afternoon, with 23 monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings on the Air Pollutant Index (API) at 4.00pm, up from 21 in the morning, according to the Department of Environment (DOE). Of the 68 stations nationwide, 23 registered readings in the unhealthy range of 101 to 200, while 39 recorded moderate air quality and six remained in the good tier. No station entered very unhealthy or hazardous territory.

items.title: Negri Sembilan education dept probing claims students served alcohol at dinner
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Education Department is finalising an investigation regarding allegations of students from a school being involved in the serving of alcoholic beverages during a dinner event held by the school's alumni association on Sept 5. In a statement today, the department said that school students should not be involved in activities involving the handling or serving of alcoholic beverages. Based on initial information, the event was organised by the alumni association outside the school premises, while the school and the association denied allegations of student involvement in the serving of alcoholic beverages , it said.

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning in 9 states until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong winds warning for nine states until 6pm today. The warning covers Perlis, Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Batang Padang and Hilir Perak), as well as Langkawi and Kubang Pasu in Kedah. The warning also applies to Kota Tinggi and Johor Baru in Johor; Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Dungun, Kemaman, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus and Setiu in Terengganu; and Jeli, Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas and Tumpat in Kelantan.

items.title: PM: Govt prepared to absorb fuel subsidy cost of up to RM45b a year
items.summary: Bernama MELAKA: The government is prepared to absorb an increase in fuel subsidy costs, which could reach RM45 billion annually amid a surge in global crude oil prices, rather than pass the burden on to the people through higher fuel prices. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government remained committed to maintaining the price of RON95 petrol at RM1.99 per litre despite international crude oil prices climbing to between US$120 and US$130 a barrel. "If oil prices continue to surge, the cost borne by the government could reach between RM42 billion and RM45 billion a year.

items.title: Melaka polls: Damian Yeo would quit politics rather than give Bemban to Bersatu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Melaka DAP chairman Damian Yeo has vowed to quit politics rather than accept any move by Pakatan Harapan (PH) to cede the Bemban state seat to Bersatu in the upcoming Melaka election. The former Duyong assemblyman said he learnt of the possibility while discussing candidates, campaign strategies and the political landscape with another former Melaka DAP chairman. Yeo said the wounds of past political betrayals remained fresh, making it difficult for him to accept any proposed cooperation with Bersatu.

items.title: Drunk driver crashes into DBKL road crew, killing supervisor on Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A road maintenance supervisor was killed and a lorry driver injured early today when a suspected drunk driver crashed into them along Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the 26-year-old driver recorded a breath alcohol level of 64mg/100ml, NST reported. The lorry driver is receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital.

items.title: Worker killed, another injured in suspected drink-driving crash in KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 28-year-old worker was killed when a drunk driver rammed his car into him while he was installing warning signs along Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar early today. The lorry driver is receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital. The car driver escaped uninjured.

items.title: End of the road: Sabah police nab Beverly Hills murder suspect wanted for over 17 years
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Oct 24 — A 42-year-old murder suspect on the run for more than 17 years has finally been arrested in Sabah over a 2009 homicide in Penampang. Penampang acting police chief Assistant Superintendent Arisanti Aziz said investigators detained the man at a house in Kolombong, Inanam on Thursday. Police had sought the suspect over the death of a man in Beverly Hills, Penampang on April 11, 2009.

items.title: 251 sexual offence cases involving tertiary students reported in 8 months
items.summary: Citing police statistics, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said the figures underscored the need for sustained efforts to improve sexual safety in educational institutions. She said the Waja Siswa Squad, part of the Women Against Crime initiative, was established to promote volunteerism and community involvement in raising awareness and addressing violence against women. Lim said violence against women and sexual harassment should not be taken lightly, as they could take various forms, including threats, humiliation, emotional manipulation, financial control and sexual abuse.

items.title: Terengganu govt extends condolences over Tengku Baderul Zaman's passing
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu state government has extended its condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire royal family following the passing of Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah today. Samsuri said the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, had decreed a three-day mourning period beginning today. Tengku Baderul Zaman, the younger brother of Sultan Mizan, died at 1.20am today at Gleneagles Hospital in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Sabah Pan Borneo 95pct complete, contractors given until year-end
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Contractors handling three critical work packages of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project along the Putatan, Penampang, Inanam, Sepanggar and Tuaran stretches have been instructed to complete the remaining construction works by the end of this year. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said completing the three packages was crucial to improving traffic flow around Kota Kinabalu and reducing congestion on existing routes. Once the Pan Borneo Highway is completed, traffic flow can be improved.

items.title: Missing man found dead in locked car at Kajang supermarket car park
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A man who went missing five days ago was found dead inside a locked car parked outside a supermarket in Jalan Impian Mahkota late last night, ending a desperate search by his family that had circulated on social media. Kajang district police chief ACP Naazron Abdul Yusof said authorities were alerted to the stationary vehicle at 11.29pm after passers-by spotted a motionless figure in the front cabin, NST reported. Naazron confirmed that the victim's family had lodged a missing person report last Tuesday after repeated attempts to reach his mobile phone went unanswered.

items.title: Sultan Sharafuddin wants no Selangor resident left behind amid state's progress
items.summary: Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said the Sultan's role as Head of the Islamic Religion in Selangor extended beyond safeguarding the faith and strengthening religious institutions to protecting the Muslim community's welfare while maintaining harmony with non-Muslims. Salehuddin said the Sultan paid particular attention to low-income Muslims and those living in poverty, insisting that they be identified so assistance could reach them effectively. Salehuddin said the Sultan had also said that state policies and budget allocations must address the housing, education and daily needs of underprivileged communities.

items.title: Anwar extends condolences to Terengganu Sultan over brother's passing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, on the passing of His Royal Highness's younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Allah SWT would shower His mercy upon Tengku Baderul Zaman's soul, grant him forgiveness and place him among the righteous. Tengku Baderul Zaman died at 1.20am today at Gleneagles Hospital.

items.title: King and Queen extend condolences to Sultan of Terengganu on brother's passing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The King, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, and the Queen, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, have extended their condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire Terengganu royal family on the passing of Sultan Mizan's younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. In a post on His Majesty's official Facebook page, the King and Queen also prayed that the late Tengku Baderul Zaman's soul be showered with barakah (divine blessings) and mercy, that all his sins be forgiven, and that he be placed among the faithful. "Condolences to Al-Wathiqu Billah Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah and the entire Terengganu Royal Family on the passing of Dato' Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah.

items.title: King and Queen offer prayers for late Terengganu prince Tengku Baderul Zaman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The King, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, and the Queen, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, have extended their condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, and the entire Terengganu royal family on the passing of Sultan Mizan’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. “Condolences to Al-Wathiqu Billah Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah and the entire Terengganu Royal Family on the passing of Dato’ Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Ibni Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. Tengku Baderul Zaman was reported to have passed away at 1.20 am today at a hospital in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Melaka polls: Wawasan wants to contest under PN logo, says Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) wants to contest the Melaka election under the Perikatan Nasional (PN) logo. Its president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the party preferred to use the coalition's logo, but would discuss alternatives if necessary. "If possible, we want to use the PN logo.

items.title: PM extends condolences to Terengganu Sultan over brother’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, on the passing of His Royal Highness’s younger brother, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman Almarhum Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah. In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Allah SWT would shower His mercy upon Tengku Baderul Zaman’s soul, grant him forgiveness and place him among the righteous. Tengku Baderul Zaman died at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital here.

items.title: BN rejects Perikatan request for additional seats in Melaka election
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 24 — Barisan Nasional (BN) will stick to its agreement to allocate seven seats it is not contesting to Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the Melaka state election, despite attempts to secure additional seats. BN chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the allocation had been agreed upon under a mutual agreement, which BN would honour. Yesterday, PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man was reported as saying that PN hoped to hold negotiations to secure an additional one or two seats in addition to the seven announced earlier.

items.title: Malaysia stands ready to assist Yemen, backs renewed negotiations
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 24 — Malaysia stands ready to deliver humanitarian assistance to Yemen, while urging all parties in the protracted conflict in the country to return to the negotiation table and look for a diplomatic solution. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia empathises with the suffering of the Yemeni people who have to endure the effects of the protracted civil war, including famine and hardship in getting basic necessities. He said the matter was brought up by his counterpart, Yemen’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Dr Afrah Abdulaziz Al-Zouba, who shared on the latest developments in the country via a phone call on Thursday.

items.title: Government to establish Veterans’ Day for MAF veterans
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The government plans to establish Veterans’ Day to honour the service and sacrifice of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) veterans. “It will also certainly foster closer ties and greater public appreciation for MAF veterans in our country,” he said at the opening ceremony of the 100th National General Assembly of the Malaysian Armed Forces Veterans Association (PVATM) here today. He said collections increased from RM1.3 million in 2023-2024 to RM2.19 million in 2024-2025 and RM3.35 million in 2025-2026.

items.title: PM Anwar calls for thorough investigation into detainee’s death in police custody
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered a thorough, transparent and uncompromising investigation into the death of Noorizwan Zulkefly in police custody. He said he understood the family’s grief and anxiety as they awaited answers regarding Noorizwan’s death. “I acknowledge the presence of the late Noorizwan’s family to submit an appeal letter to me today.

items.title: New-generation MyKad records 275,785 issuances in first month
items.summary: KULAI, Oct 24 — The National Registration Department (JPN) has issued 275,785 new-generation MyKad nationwide since its launch on Sept 17 until Oct 20, with Johor recording the highest number at 31,392 cards. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures reflected a positive response from the public to the new-generation MyKad, which comes with enhanced security features. He said the new-generation MyKad incorporates 53 security features, compared with 23 in the previous version, including a transparent window, QR code, ultraviolet features, hologram and microtext.

items.title: Cheras custodial death: Family takes plea to PM’s doorstep, seeks transparent probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The family of Noorizwan Zulkefly, who died earlier this month while under the custody of the Cheras district police, brought their fight for justice directly to the prime minister's doorstep this morning, demanding an independent and transparent inquiry into the circumstances surrounding his death. The memorandum, handed over by Noorizwan's younger brother Nooranis Zulkefly, expressed profound alarm over unexplained physical injuries documented during the post-mortem examination, urging Putrajaya to intervene directly to prevent an institutional cover-up. Pathologists at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) in Cheras confirmed that while the post-mortem detected no structural trauma to internal organs, Noorizwan's body bore multiple external contusions and injuries.

items.title: Police probe local syndicate links after Indonesia seizes tanker carrying RM800m ketamine off Sumatra
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Federal narcotics investigators are working in close concert with Indonesian law enforcement to determine whether a Malaysian drug syndicate orchestrated the trafficking of 1.16 tonnes of ketamine hydrochloride aboard a coastal tanker intercepted off North Sumatra. The 57-metre Mongolian-flagged vessel, MT Global 168, was intercepted off Tanjung Balai Asahan on October 20 after Indonesian authorities linked its registered ownership to Johor-based firm Makmur Marine Petroleum. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan confirmed that Malaysian police were formally notified of the massive maritime interdiction by Indonesian counterparts yesterday, NST reported.

items.title: Kedah, Penang, Perak, Melaka, Johor and Sarawak put on thunderstorm alert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has sounded a midday thunderstorm advisory for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, warning of torrential rain, lightning, and gusty winds until 2.00pm today. In Kedah, stormy conditions are expected across eight districts, namely Kota Setar, Pendang, Yan, Kuala Muda, Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Baling, and Sik. Affected zones include Sebuyau in the Samarahan division, alongside Pantu, Lingga, and Sri Aman within the Sri Aman division, and Betong.

items.title: Wisma Putra: Two Malaysians suffer minor injuries after Typhoon Champi in Taiwan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Two Malaysian nationals are currently receiving medical treatment for minor injuries in the aftermath of Typhoon Champi on Taiwan, the Foreign Ministry said. The ministry which is also known as Wisma Putra said the matter was confirmed by the Malaysian Friendship and Trade Centre in Taipei, which is also providing the necessary consular assistance to both individuals. — BERNAMA TAGS: Typhoon Champi, Taiwan, Wisma Putra, consular assistance

items.title: Perikatan seeks talks with Perlis MB Abu Bakar snookered by two-term Bersatu suspension
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) leadership is aiming to broker a resolution to the political crisis in Perlis, seeking direct talks with Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah following his two-term suspension from Bersatu. Takiyuddin, who also serves as PAS secretary-general, noted that while Bersatu's disciplinary board had frozen Abu Bakar's party rights, the embattled state chief technically remains a Bersatu member. He noted that this restricts Abu Bakar from seeking refuge outside of Bersatu.

items.title: Sultan Mizan’s brother passes away; Terengganu declares three-day mourning
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 24 — The younger brother of the Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, Datuk Seri Dr Tengku Baderul Zaman, son of the late Sultan Mahmud Al-Muktafi Billah Shah, passed away at 1.20 am today at Gleneagles Hospital, Kuala Lumpur. According to a statement by the Comptroller of the Terengganu Royal Household, Datuk Mohd Sophian Abu Bakar, the remains of Tengku Baderul Zaman will arrive at Sultan Mahmud Airport in Kuala Nerus at 1.15pm aboard a special aircraft. The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail, will receive the remains of the late Tengku Baderul Zaman.

items.title: Sultan Sharafuddin calls for AI training, responsible social media use, geriatric care for Selangor’s future
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — The Sultan of Selangor hopes future generations of Selangorians will be knowledgeable, compassionate, resilient, united and respectful of others. His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah said young people should strive for excellence without losing their sense of responsibility towards society. Sultan Sharafuddin said the younger generation had rightly placed importance on environmental sustainability and heritage preservation.

items.title: Monarchy provides stability above political differences, says Selangor Sultan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Although society has evolved, the fundamental role of a constitutional monarch remains unchanged, the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, said. Sultan Sharafuddin said the Constitution provided clear guidance on his responsibilities. The monarchy, he said, represented continuity, stability, service and responsibility.

items.title: Bukit Aman: Post-mortem finds external injuries in Cheras custodial death, cause of death pending lab analysis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — A post-mortem conducted on a 42-year-old man who died following detention by Cheras police revealed no damage to his internal organs but confirmed multiple external bodily injuries, federal investigators said today. Today’s police statement acknowledged the external injuries but stopped short of describing their severity, nature, or likely origin. To ensure independent oversight, JIPS confirmed that the case has been formally referred to the Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) under Section 26 of the Independent Police Conduct Commission Act 2022, fulfilling mandatory reporting statutory requirements for fatalities in custody.

items.title: Haze creeps back: Seremban and Johor’s Larkin log highest API readings at 169
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 24 — Air quality deteriorated across several states this morning, with 21 monitoring stations breaching unhealthy thresholds on the Air Pollutant Index (API), according to the Department of Environment (DOE). Data from the DOE's environmental monitoring dashboard at 10.00am showed that nearly a third of the country's 68 air quality stations registered readings between 101 and 200. Another 41 stations recorded moderate air quality, while only six maintained good air levels.
